featured.title: Trump Pauses 50% Canadian Tariffs After Preliminary Trade Deal
featured.content: U.S. President Donald Trump has announced a temporary pause on planned 50% tariffs on certain Canadian goods after saying the United States and Canada had reached a preliminary agreement. The announcement follows intense negotiations between Washington and Ottawa and could provide temporary relief for businesses on both sides of the border. Reuters reports that the pause is for three days while the two countries continue working through remaining trade issues.

articles.title: Trump–Canada Trade Dispute Enters New Phase
articles.description: The United States has temporarily paused planned 50% tariffs on certain Canadian imports after President Donald Trump announced that Washington and Ottawa had reached a preliminary deal. The pause follows prolonged negotiations and gives both governments additional time to work toward a broader trade agreement.

articles.title: Spain Hit By More Earthquakes
articles.description: Three further earthquakes struck southern Spain's Granada province, causing light injuries and damage to buildings. Authorities restricted access to parts of the historic Alhambra complex while safety assessments continued. The latest tremors followed a stronger earthquake in the region several days earlier.

articles.title: South Korea And US Scale Back Military Exercises
articles.description: South Korea and the United States have agreed to shorten and reduce the scope of their annual joint military exercises. North Korea has criticized the drills, while Seoul and Washington continue to describe them as defensive.

articles.title: China's Wang Yi Visits South Korea
articles.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi begins a two-day visit to South Korea as Beijing and Seoul discuss regional security, diplomatic relations and wider developments affecting East Asia.

articles.title: Ukraine War Remains A Major Security Concern
articles.description: Russia's war against Ukraine remains a major international security issue. Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure and Ukrainian strikes against targets inside Russia continue to keep European governments focused on security assistance, sanctions and diplomatic efforts.

articles.title: Iran–US Tensions Continue To Affect Global Security
articles.description: Tensions involving Iran, the United States and the Strait of Hormuz continue to affect international security and energy markets. Shipping activity through the strategic waterway has slowed significantly, increasing concerns about energy supplies and global transportation.

articles.title: US Lifts Security Restrictions On Nigerian Ships
articles.description: The United States has lifted security restrictions imposed on vessels arriving from Nigeria after more than 12 years. Nigerian authorities expect the decision to reduce shipping costs and strengthen the competitiveness of Nigerian ports.

articles.title: Plateau State Attack Leaves At Least 24 Dead
articles.description: At least 24 people were reported killed after gunmen attacked the Bin-Per community in Plateau State, Nigeria. Authorities are investigating the incident and working to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Becomes Country's Deadliest
articles.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the country's deadliest recorded outbreak. Reuters reports that 2,325 deaths and 4,945 confirmed cases had been recorded by August 16. Health authorities and international organizations are continuing containment and response operations.

articles.title: Nigeria Continues Focus On Economic Growth
articles.description: Nigeria continues to focus on investment, energy production, infrastructure and economic reforms as government officials seek stronger growth and improved opportunities for businesses and households.

articles.title: Europe Faces Continuing Climate Pressure
articles.description: Europe continues to experience the effects of extreme heat and changing weather patterns. Scientists say human-caused climate change was the main driver of recent record-breaking sea temperatures around Europe, raising concerns for marine ecosystems and coastal communities.

articles.title: European Wildfire And Heat Risks Continue
articles.description: Several European countries continue monitoring wildfire and extreme-weather risks following a summer marked by heat, drought and dangerous fire conditions. Emergency services remain on alert in areas vulnerable to fires and heat-related disruption.

articles.title: Global Markets Watch Trade And Geopolitical Risks
articles.description: Investors are monitoring the latest US–Canada trade developments alongside geopolitical tensions, energy prices, inflation expectations and monetary policy. The temporary pause on Canadian tariffs could provide some relief to markets while negotiations continue.

articles.title: US Dollar Remains Under Pressure
articles.description: The US dollar remains near multi-month lows as investors assess economic data and await further signals from the Federal Reserve. Geopolitical uncertainty and energy-market movements remain important factors for currency markets.

articles.title: Oil Markets Continue Watching Strait Of Hormuz
articles.description: Energy traders continue monitoring the Strait of Hormuz because disruption to shipping through the waterway could affect global oil supplies and transportation costs. Oil prices remain sensitive to developments involving Iran and regional security.

articles.title: China's Unitree Robotics Attracts Global Attention
articles.description: Chinese robotics company Unitree is attracting international attention with its humanoid robotics technology as China's robotics industry expands. Competition in humanoid machines is becoming an increasingly important part of the global technology race.

articles.title: AI Investment Remains A Global Priority
articles.description: Technology companies and investors continue directing enormous amounts of capital toward artificial intelligence infrastructure, computing power, data centres and advanced AI systems. Governments are simultaneously working on regulation, safety and digital skills.

articles.title: Nigeria Looks To Expand Artificial Intelligence Skills
articles.description: Nigeria continues exploring partnerships and training initiatives aimed at expanding artificial intelligence skills among young people and technology professionals. Digital education and access to advanced technology remain important parts of the country's economic-development strategy.

articles.title: Climate Change And Public Health Remain Global Challenges
articles.description: Extreme weather, infectious disease outbreaks and environmental changes continue challenging governments and international organizations. Experts are calling for stronger preparedness, early-warning systems and international cooperation.

articles.title: International Diplomacy Remains In Focus
articles.description: Governments around the world continue diplomatic efforts involving wars, trade disputes, security arrangements, migration, climate change and international economic cooperation.

articles.title: Today's Big Question
articles.description: If trade tensions, security threats, climate change and public-health emergencies continue to grow, which challenge should world leaders tackle first? Tell us your view in the comments.

articles.title: Quote Of The Day
articles.description: The truth may travel slowly, but informed minds never stop looking for it.
